articles.summary: Việt Nam-Singapore digital ID link: a test for ASEAN interoperability  vietnamnews.vn
articles.full_text:
| Việt Nam's national electronic identification application, VNeID, on a mobile phone. The application is going to be connected to Singapore's Singpass and Laos' LAeID systems. — VNA/VNS Photo | 
SINGAPORE — Việt Nam is advancing plans to connect its national electronic identification application, VNeID, with Singapore’s Singpass system and Laos’s LAeID system under Decision No. 1830/QD-TTg dated September 22, 2026, issued by the Prime Minister, with trial connectivity targeted for completion before November 15, 2026.
This high-tech initiative marks an important step towards simplifying administrative procedures and immigration formalities, while promoting digital cooperation within ASEAN.
From Singapore’s perspective, connecting VNeID with Singpass could lay the foundation for a bilateral digital corridor, opening up greater opportunities for cooperation in trade, investment, services, tourism and finance.
Singapore has operated its Singpass digital identity system since 2003, while Việt Nam is stepping up the development of its national population database and the use of VNeID.
Professor Vũ Minh Khương from the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy emphasised that connecting digital infrastructure, especially between Việt Nam and Singapore, should be a top priority.
He noted that the Việt Nam-Singapore-Laos connectivity model is a foundation for expanding electronic interoperability across the region, covering areas like customs, tourism, payments, banking, and finance.
"To make this vision a reality, businesses must develop platform models, identify needs and coordinate implementation," he said.
For citizens, digital ID interoperability could simplify information verification, reduce repetitive declaration requirements, and shorten the time needed to complete administrative procedures.
Businesses could also benefit from convenient identity verification when opening bank accounts, registering businesses, or establishing legal entities across borders.
However, the connectivity process poses a number of technical, security, and legal challenges.
According to Lê Anh Đức, an artificial intelligence (AI) expert and Vice Chairman and Head of the Science and Technology Committee of the Liaison Committee for the Vietnamese Community in Singapore, the two countries need to address differences in data structures, develop standards for information mapping, and ensure stable connectivity.
"In particular, cross-border data exchange must meet requirements for privacy protection and information security, while preventing identity fraud and cyberattacks," Đức said.
At the ASEAN level, further obstacles include disparities in technological development among member states, differences in digital signature standards, and variations in legal frameworks for personal data protection, he added. Therefore, establishing compatible standards and lawful data-sharing mechanisms is crucial to expanding the model.
The trial connection of VNeID with Singpass and LAeID could serve as a pilot model for testing technical and legal solutions before wider implementation.
If implemented effectively, the initiative would help promote digital identity interoperability, facilitate cross-border transactions, and support ASEAN’s digital integration process. — VNA/VNS

articles.title: Indonesia-Canada trade deal set to boost exports in December - ANTARA News
articles.summary: Indonesia-Canada trade deal set to boost exports in December  ANTARA News
articles.full_text:
Menteri Perdagangan (Mendag) Budi Santoso (ANTARA/HO-Kemendag)
“We hope that Indonesian businesses will take advantage of the various facilities and opportunities created by this agreement to boost exports, expand market reach, and strengthen the competitiveness of Indonesian products in the international market,” Santoso said in Jakarta on Thursday.
The I-CA CEPA marks Indonesia’s first bilateral trade agreement with a partner in North America and Canada’s first bilateral trade agreement with a country in Southeast Asia.
The agreement will take effect following the exchange of notifications confirming the completion of ratification procedures by both countries.
Canada submitted its notification on October 1, 2026, followed by Indonesia on October 20, 2026. Under the I-CA CEPA, Canada will liberalize 90.55 percent of its tariff lines for Indonesian products.
Santoso expects the preferential tariff arrangements to make Indonesian goods more price-competitive and create opportunities for exporters to expand their presence in the Canadian market.
However, he urged businesses to pay close attention to tariff reduction schedules, rules of origin, and Canada’s technical requirements and regulations.
Johni Martha, the Trade Ministry’s director general of international trade negotiations, emphasized that businesses, including micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), need to prepare for exporting to Canada.
Preparations include identifying market opportunities in Canada, ensuring products meet applicable requirements, and exploring business partnerships with prospective buyers and other potential partners.
From January to August 2026, bilateral trade between Indonesia and Canada reached US$3.51 billion, up 15.50 percent from US$3.04 billion in the same period a year earlier. During the same period, Indonesia’s exports to Canada totaled US$1.12 billion, while imports from Canada reached US$2.39 billion.
In 2025, bilateral trade between the two countries reached US$4.36 billion, up from US$3.58 billion in 2024.
Indonesia’s exports to Canada totaled US$1.70 billion in 2025, while imports from Canada amounted to US$2.67 billion.
Indonesia’s main exports to Canada include electrical machinery and equipment, rubber and rubber products, footwear, knitted goods, and apparel.
Meanwhile, Indonesia imports wheat, fertilizers, wood pulp, mineral fuels, salt, sulfur, and lime from Canada.

articles.title: When imports grow faster than exports: How can we transform investment capital into domestic value? - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: When imports grow faster than exports: How can we transform investment capital into domestic value?  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
(CLO) The majority of Vietnam's imports are machinery, equipment, and raw materials for production. However, with imports growing faster than exports, the challenge is how to transform this investment flow into domestic value and boost exports.
A trade deficit isn't necessarily a negative thing.
According to a report by the General Statistics Office of the Ministry of Finance , in the first nine months of 2026, Vietnam's export turnover reached US$434.30 billion, an increase of 24.5% compared to the same period last year. Meanwhile, imports increased by 36.7%, to US$452.72 billion, resulting in a trade deficit of US$19.42 billion.
However, the sharp increase in imports is not entirely a negative sign. The majority of imported goods are machinery, equipment, and raw materials for production, indicating that the investment cycle in Vietnam is still ongoing.
Specifically, in the first nine months of the year, production materials accounted for 94.1% of total import turnover, of which machinery, equipment, tools and spare parts accounted for 58.3%. During the same period, asset accumulation in the third quarter increased by 21.39%, and the manufacturing production index increased by 12.9%. Realized FDI reached US$21.07 billion, of which 82.6% was concentrated in the manufacturing sector.
According to EBC Financial Group (EBC), these figures show a relatively clear link between imports of production materials, investment expansion, and industrial production growth. Imported machinery, equipment, and raw materials are contributing to increasing the production capacity of the economy .
However, increased imports do not necessarily mean that every dollar spent generates a corresponding economic benefit. The effectiveness of investment also depends on the level of capacity utilization, labor productivity, the proportion of value created domestically, and the ability to sell products in the international market.
"Ultimate effectiveness depends on capacity utilization, productivity, value created domestically, and the ability of global demand to absorb new output," the EBC report stated.
One notable issue is that the benefits from the new investment cycle have not been evenly distributed among economic sectors. In the first nine months of the year, the domestic economic sector recorded a trade deficit of $34.28 billion, while the FDI sector recorded a trade surplus of $14.86 billion.
According to EBC, this disparity poses a long-term problem: production capacity may increase rapidly, but the economy may not necessarily benefit proportionally if domestic businesses do not participate deeply in supply chains, technology, services, and high value-added stages.
In other words, expanding factories and increasing capacity is only the first step. For the investment cycle to yield sustainable results, Vietnamese businesses need to improve their supply capacity, enhance productivity, and increase the proportion of value created domestically, thereby increasing their ability to participate in production and export chains.
"A more sustainable investment cycle therefore needs to be accompanied by higher productivity, greater export capacity, and an improved rate of domestic value added," EBC stated.
You may also like
Therefore, according to EBC, evaluating the next phase of the investment cycle cannot be based solely on the amount of imported machinery and equipment or the scale of capital injected into the economy. What is important is how much output, domestic value, and foreign exchange earnings these resources generate.
If exports gradually catch up with the pace of import growth as new capacity comes online, the current trade deficit may reflect the investment process for future production expansion. Conversely, if the new production capacity has not yet been converted into export revenue and added value, the pressure on capital and the balance of payments will be more significant.
Rising costs are putting increasing pressure on businesses.
Besides the challenge of investment efficiency, the cost of maintaining growth momentum is also becoming a major concern for the business community.
According to the General Statistics Office, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) in September increased by 5.08% compared to the same period last year, bringing the average CPI increase for the first nine months to 4.52%. Meanwhile, the price index of raw materials, fuels, and supplies used in production increased by 5.12%, indicating that cost pressures remain present at the input levels of the economy.
Manufacturing activity continued to expand, but the momentum showed signs of slowing. The manufacturing PMI fell from 53.3 points in August to 51.9 points in September. The pace of new orders slowed, export orders weakened, while input costs increased and delivery times lengthened.
According to EBC, these developments could put pressure on profit margins, working capital requirements, inventory financing costs, and imported raw material prices for manufacturing businesses. As input costs rise, businesses may need more capital to maintain the same scale of operations, putting further pressure on the efficiency of production expansion.
Sana Ur Rehman, Senior Market Analyst at EBC Financial Group, commented: "The Q3 GDP shows that Vietnam's investment cycle is generating real output."
"However, September manufacturing data suggests that to maintain this pace, businesses may have to operate in a more challenging cost environment. Therefore, the quality and efficiency of growth are becoming increasingly important," he said.
From now until the end of the year, EBC believes there are five indicators that need to be monitored to assess the effectiveness of the investment cycle and the resilience of the economy.
Firstly, the question is whether the export growth rate is narrowing the gap with imports, thereby demonstrating the ability to convert new capacity into revenue from international markets.
You may also like
Secondly, will export orders in the manufacturing sector recover after showing signs of weakness in September?
Third, will industrial production continue to grow in proportion to the additional production capacity generated by new investments?
Fourth, the pressure from rising input costs and inflation has eased, helping businesses reduce their cost burdens.
Fifth, will access to capital and exchange rates remain stable amidst continued high demand for investment and imports?
According to EBC, the sharp increase in imports has contributed to boosting investment and expanding production. However, the next phase will show whether this momentum can generate more sustainable growth driven by productivity, exports, and domestic value-added, or whether it will remain increasingly dependent on capital, imported goods, and foreign exchange.
Vietnam's challenge, therefore, is not only to maintain investment momentum, but also to improve the efficiency of capital utilization, increase the participation of domestic enterprises in supply chains, and ensure new production capacity to create commensurate value for the economy.

ISTANBUL – Leaders of the four Quad nations will convene next month on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit in the Philippines, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday.
“It’s been agreement now that we’re going to do it; we’re going to do it in Manila, at the ASEAN conference,” Rubio told Indian broadcaster CNN-News18.
He said there was no specific date yet, “but that’s going to happen, and we’re very enthusiastic about it.” The 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit is scheduled for Nov. 16-18 in Manila.
Rubio said the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue, comprising the US, Australia, India and Japan, was gaining momentum, adding that the upcoming meeting would go beyond a standard diplomatic encounter.
He emphasized that the gathering aims to deliver substantive results, noting that member states intend to announce “concrete actions, not just simply a nice social gathering, but something that has concrete deliverables.”
The planned gathering will mark the first leaders’ summit of the diplomatic partnership since September 2024. India originally held the rotation to host the dialogue, but scheduling challenges delayed the meeting.
US President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit Manila and Shenzhen in November, attending ASEAN-related meetings in the Philippines before traveling to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting on Nov. 18-19, where he is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping. articles.title: Improving the quality of export growth - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Improving the quality of export growth  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Exports maintained their upward trend, but imports increased even faster, causing a reversal in the trade balance. Pressure from international markets and dependence on imported raw materials are creating a need for Vietnamese businesses to enhance their competitiveness.
A garment company received additional export orders for the year-end shopping season. While this seemed like an opportunity to increase revenue, recalculating the costs of raw materials, transportation, and labor revealed that the projected profit margin was significantly reduced. Accepting the orders meant increasing production, but maintaining profitability proved to be the real challenge.
This story reflects the pressure many export businesses are facing in the final months of 2026. With demand in major markets recovering unevenly, and raw material prices and logistics costs fluctuating, export businesses must not only ensure timely delivery but also find ways to maintain competitiveness.
In Thanh Hoa , many businesses are focusing their resources on fulfilling signed orders. However, fluctuations in raw material prices, transportation costs, and tariff policies in major markets are causing considerable difficulties for export activities. Ms. Hoang Thi Kim Dung, Vice President of the Thanh Hoa Textile and Garment Association, said that to retain orders, businesses must reduce costs, increase productivity, and proactively organize production.

Meanwhile, businesses exporting agricultural, forestry, and aquatic products are also facing pressure from quality standards, food safety, traceability, and requirements for stable supply. Mr. Le Quy Viet, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Thanh Hoa Aquatic Products Import-Export Joint Stock Company, believes that improving internal capacity, production efficiency, and the ability to meet international standards are decisive factors in maintaining market share and developing orders.
These difficulties partly reflect the general challenges facing Vietnam's export activities, as export turnover continues to increase but cost pressures and dependence on imported raw materials are growing.
According to the Customs Department, in the first 15 days of October 2026, total import and export turnover reached US$56.68 billion, an increase of 48.5% compared to the same period last year. Cumulative import and export turnover up to October 15th exceeded US$945 billion, of which exports reached US$463.7 billion and imports US$481.36 billion.
Previously, in the first nine months of 2026, total import and export turnover reached 888 billion USD, an increase of 30.4%. Export turnover reached 434.3 billion USD, an increase of 25.4%, while import turnover reached 453.7 billion USD, an increase of 36.7%.
Imports increased faster than exports, causing the trade balance to shift from a surplus of $16.87 billion in the same period of 2025 to a deficit of $19.4 billion.
You may also like
Notably, the electronics sector contributed over 42% of total export turnover but also had a large trade deficit. In the first nine months, imports of computers, electronic products, and components reached $188.9 billion, an increase of 71.7%, while exports reached $123.6 billion, a difference of over $65 billion.
Explaining the reasons, Ms. Trinh Thi Thu Hien, Deputy Director of the Import-Export Department ( Ministry of Industry and Trade ), said that the price of raw materials for electronics and semiconductor production has increased sharply, with some types of chips and SSDs increasing by 300-500%, pushing up the import value.
Along with that, the demand for raw materials to produce technology products, especially artificial intelligence (AI), is increasing rapidly, forcing businesses to increase their inventory. Some businesses have extended their inventory holding period from 6 to 12 weeks, and the value of inventory for many businesses has even increased from $100 million to $700 million.
The wave of investment expansion by corporations such as Samsung , Intel, and BYD has also driven up the demand for importing machinery, equipment, and components for production.
From an operational perspective, Mr. Bui Huy Son, Director of the Planning and Finance Department (Ministry of Industry and Trade), noted that industrial production and exports continued to grow positively, but the quality of growth was uneven.
Notably, the foreign direct investment (FDI) sector accounted for 80.9% of total export turnover, increasing by 29.2%, while domestic enterprises only increased by 6.1%. This shows that export growth still heavily depends on the FDI sector, while the capacity of domestic enterprises to participate in supply chains remains limited.
Enhancing domestic value for sustainable growth.
According to Ms. Trinh Thi Thu Hien, to reduce the trade deficit, it is first necessary to maintain the growth momentum of exports. However, imports also need to be viewed in relation to the demand for raw materials, machinery, and components for production.
The Ministry of Industry and Trade is implementing solutions to support businesses in expanding markets, boosting exports, and simultaneously enhancing domestic production capacity, increasing the localization rate and added value in the supply chain.
This is also a key orientation in the draft Strategy for Goods Export and Import to 2030, with a vision to 2045. Accordingly, in the period 2026-2030, exports are expected to increase by an average of 15-16% per year, imports by 12-13% per year, and a sustainable trade surplus of 3-6% of total export turnover is to be maintained. By 2045, Vietnam aims to be among the top 10 countries with the largest export and import turnover in the world , with a trade surplus ratio of 7-10%.
You may also like
Notably, the strategy aims to increase the export share of domestic enterprises to 28-30% by 2030 and 38-40% by 2045. The proportion of processed or refined goods is targeted to reach 89-90% by 2030 and over 92% by 2045.
In terms of scale, the draft proposes three export scenarios by 2030, ranging from $765 billion to $1,041.1 billion.
These objectives show that export growth cannot rely solely on expanding markets or increasing orders. More importantly, it requires developing supporting industries, enhancing the capacity of domestic businesses, and increasing the technological content of products.
In the short term, maintaining export momentum will contribute to improving the trade balance. But in the long term, reducing dependence on imported raw materials, increasing the export share of domestic enterprises, and retaining more value in the supply chain are the foundations for the sustainable development of Vietnam's exports.

articles.title: Quang Ninh prioritizes attracting high-quality FDI to promote sustainable growth. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Quang Ninh prioritizes attracting high-quality FDI to promote sustainable growth.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
With its advantageous geographical location, increasingly完善 infrastructure system, and efforts to improve the business environment, Quang Ninh is continuing to affirm its attractiveness to foreign investors.
 The city not only focuses on attracting new projects but also creates favorable conditions for existing businesses to expand production and operations, gradually improving the quality of foreign direct investment (FDI), serving the goal of modern and sustainable economic development.
 According to the Quang Ninh City Electronic Information Portal, in the first nine months of 2026, Quang Ninh attracted US$1,349.5 million in FDI. Of this, the locality issued new investment registration certificates for 26 projects with a total registered capital of US$659.68 million; and recorded 85 project adjustments, including 22 capital increases totaling US$689.66 million. This result demonstrates the attractiveness of the investment environment, not only in its ability to attract new projects but also in the confidence of investors already operating in the area.
 By sector, the processing and manufacturing industry continued to play a leading role, attracting $842.87 million, accounting for 62.5% of total FDI. The real estate sector ranked second with $494.98 million, equivalent to 36.7%. Notably, industrial parks and economic zones continued to be key areas, attracting $1,303.85 million, accounting for 96.6% of the province's total foreign investment during the period.
 Many industrial parks have become destinations for large-scale investors. The Song Khoai Industrial Park currently attracts 25 secondary projects with a total registered capital of approximately US$3.35 billion, while the Bac Tien Phong Industrial Park has 38 projects with a total capital of approximately US$3.1 billion. The presence and expansion of corporations such as Foxconn, Jinko Solar, Yaskawa, Tonly Electronics, etc., contribute to increased industrial production capacity and open up opportunities for the development of high-tech and high-value-added industries.
 In reality, besides preferential policies, investors are increasingly interested in the quality of infrastructure, access to clean land, transportation connectivity, and the ease of project implementation.
 Recognizing this, Quang Ninh is focusing on removing bottlenecks in land acquisition, accelerating infrastructure investment in industrial parks and economic zones, and strengthening efforts to urge infrastructure investors to adhere to their plans. The list of projects attracting non-budgetary investment for the 2026-2030 period is also being reviewed and updated to proactively approach investors with strong financial and technological capabilities and long-term development orientations.
 Along with infrastructure improvements, investment promotion activities are being implemented in a focused and targeted manner. The locality proactively reviews priority projects and strengthens contact with corporations and businesses that hold important positions in the international supply chain. Emphasis is also placed on leveraging the existing FDI network, thereby creating additional channels for connecting, introducing investment opportunities, and reinforcing the confidence of new investors in the business environment in Quang Ninh.
 Administrative reform continues to be one of the key solutions to reduce time and costs and facilitate business operations. In the first nine months of 2026, the locality simplified the required documents for 59 out of 59 specific administrative procedures; at the same time, it announced the reduction and replacement of required documents with data for 539 administrative procedures under various ministries and agencies for implementation in the locality. 
 The effectiveness of the reforms is also reflected in the results of handling applications at public administrative service centers. The city's Public Administrative Service Center processed 256,475 applications, of which 255,196 were processed on time or ahead of schedule, achieving a rate of 99.5%. At the commune, ward, and special zone-level public administrative service centers, the number of applications processed reached 379,395, with 372,311 processed on time or ahead of schedule, equivalent to 98.1%. In addition, functional agencies have strengthened support for businesses in the process of site surveying, completing investment, land, construction, environmental procedures, and project implementation.
 During the period 2026-2030, Quang Ninh aims to attract at least US$15 billion in registered FDI capital, with a total implemented capital of at least US$12.71 billion. To realize this goal, the investment attraction strategy is selective, prioritizing sectors such as electronics, automation, logistics, seaports, green economy, digital infrastructure, and high-end tourism . Projects are encouraged to utilize modern technology, use resources efficiently, reduce emissions, create high added value, and be linked to technology transfer, human resource training, and strengthening connections with domestic businesses.
 Besides attracting new capital, the locality also focuses on improving the efficiency of using existing investment resources. Reviewing projects that are slow to implement or no longer feasible will contribute to improving the efficiency of land use and avoiding resource waste. At the same time, strengthening connections between FDI enterprises and domestic enterprises is considered an important solution to expand opportunities to participate in supply chains, enhance technological capabilities, and promote the development of the local industrial ecosystem.
 With a selective investment attraction strategy focused on quality and efficiency, coupled with efforts to improve infrastructure, reform administrative procedures, and support businesses, Quang Ninh is gradually consolidating its position in attracting FDI. This not only provides a foundation for the locality to achieve its investment capital targets in the coming years but also contributes to transforming international resources into a driving force for industrial development, enhancing competitiveness, and promoting sustainable economic growth.

A single export application for research and development purposes has been permitted by the mineral and geoscience department, the natural resources ministry said in response to a Bloomberg query. It did not identify the applicant or provide details.
Rare earths are among the most critical raw materials on the planet, deeply embedded in the technologies that underpin modern life, including an array of key defence applications. While China has long dominated their mining and processing, other nations including Malaysia are now stepping up efforts to develop their own capacity in a push to reduce reliance on Beijing.
At present, the Southeast Asian nation hosts Australia’s Lynas Rare Earths Ltd, one of only two major producers outside China, with local conglomerates including Berjaya Corp Bhd also exploring projects.
Among other overseas companies, France’s Carester SAS plans to build a rare-earths separation plant in the northern state of Perak with Malaysia’s Malaco Mining Group, and more than a dozen US firms are also exploring local opportunities.
Earlier this month, Malaysia released guidelines for the conditional export of raw rare earths, easing a moratorium that had been in place since 2024. Under the revised framework, shipments of unprocessed materials can be permitted for research and development or processing, subject to conditions.
“The guidelines are open to eligible applicants, including foreign companies, subject to compliance with the relevant regulatory requirements,” the ministry said. The priority is not the number of applications approved, but quality of investments, technology transfer and long-term value creation, it added.

articles.title: TSH Resources says 274 hotspots detected within estate boundaries were outside operational areas - CNA
articles.summary: TSH Resources says 274 hotspots detected within estate boundaries were outside operational areas  CNAMalaysia demands effective action from Indonesia on transboundary haze  NST OnlineTSH Resources reports 274 hot spots within estate boundaries after SGX queries over haze  The Business TimesMalaysia expects tourism fallout from Indonesia haze  Yahoo News SingaporeBersatu MP speaks Javanese to ensure Prabowo 'understands' haze crisis demands  Malay...
articles.full_text:
The palm oil cultivation company said the hotspots detected within its estate between January and Oct 21 were in “community enclave areas”.
SINGAPORE: Palm oil cultivation company TSH Resources said on Thursday (Oct 22) that 274 hotspots detected within its estate between January and Oct 21 were in “community enclave areas” outside its operational areas.
The company was responding to queries from the Singapore Exchange (SGX) about whether its operations had contributed to the recent haze in Southeast Asia.
In a bourse filing, TSH Resources said no fire was detected within its planted or operational areas between January and Oct 21.
There was also no report or claim of fires started by its employees, it added.
“During the period, 274 hotspots were detected within the group's estate boundaries and were all in community enclave areas, outside the group's operational areas,” said TSH Resources.
The company said its field teams responded to and extinguished the fires, and lodged police reports for the incidents.
It also disclosed that a fire broke out on Aug 17 within the Hak Guna Usaha area of its subsidiary, PT Bulungan Citra Agro Persada (BCAP).
“The fire originated from a community enclave area outside BCAP's operational area. BCAP extinguished the fire on the same day, lodged a police report and continues to cooperate with the relevant authorities,” TSH Resources said.
The company, which operates oil palm plantations and mills in Malaysia and Indonesia, maintained that its operations and activities within its Indonesian concessions had not contributed to the recent haze.
Senior Minister K Shanmugam had warned this week that Singapore would use every legal, regulatory and economic lever at its disposal against companies responsible for the haze.
The country has been facing stretches of unhealthy air quality due to the haze since Sep 4. At least one region in Singapore had unhealthy air quality from Oct 5 until Thursday afternoon.
Mr Shanmugam said that the SGX had asked questions of seven agri-companies listed in Singapore.
Besides TSH Resources, the other companies are Golden Agri-Resources, Bumitama Agri, First Resources, Wilmar International, Kencana Agri and Indofood Agri.
Kencana Agri said in response last week that Indonesian authorities have launched a preliminary inquiry into a fire incident at its subsidiary.
First Resources said on Tuesday that it welcomes on-the-ground inspections by the authorities as well as documentary and technical reviews, adding that it fully supports a "thorough, evidence-based examination of facts" into the ongoing haze situation.
COMPANY SAYS OPERATIONS DID NOT CONTRIBUTE TO HAZE
According to its SGX profile page, TSH Resources has oil palm plantations and palm oil mill in Sabah, Malaysia, as well as Kalimantan and Sumatera in Indonesia.
Among SGX’s questions were whether the company's operations had contributed to the haze and whether it had received any allegations or enquiries about the recent fires in Indonesia or the haze.
TSH Resources said it had not been named or issued any notices by environmental agencies in connection with the recent transboundary haze.
It also shared that it received an enquiry from its customer, Apical Group, on Sep 1 about hotspots in PT Farinda Bersaudara, one of its subsidiaries.
PT Farinda Bersaudara was acquired by TSH Resources in 2008, according to the latter’s website.
The company said it had clarified that the hotspots occurred within community enclaves outside its operational area.
“Apical was satisfied with our clarification,” it added.
TSH Resources did not receive any other official enquiries and there were no media highlights about the company as of Oct 15, it said.
MEASURES IN PLACE
TSH Resources said it enforces a zero-burning policy across its operations, including land preparation, new planting and replanting.
The policy also extends to its contractors and suppliers, it added.
The company said it has fire prevention and emergency response measures in place, including regular ground patrols, trained firefighting teams and satellite monitoring.
“TSH's in-house LiTUP system integrates multiple satellite data sources to monitor hotspots within concession boundaries and a 2km-buffer zone, providing updates approximately every three hours to support early detection and timely response,” it added.
The company said it also maintains its firefighting infrastructure, equipment and trained squads in accordance with legal standards in Indonesia.
Its Indonesian estates are certified under the Indonesian Sustainable Palm Oil scheme, which is subject to regular third-party audits.
The company said it had put in place the necessary measures to prevent, monitor and respond to fires, and did not consider further disclosure necessary as there had been no incident with a material impact on the group.

articles.title: Singapore sets aside $45m to help advanced manufacturing SMEs use AI solutions - The Straits Times
articles.summary: Singapore sets aside $45m to help advanced manufacturing SMEs use AI solutions  The Straits Times
articles.full_text:
AI generated
SINGAPORE – More than $45 million has been set aside over the next three years to help small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the advanced manufacturing industry deploy artificial intelligence solutions.
This is one of the initiatives under Singapore’s national AI strategy that were announced by Minister of State for Energy, Trade and Industry Gan Siow Huang on Oct 21.
Gan said the Catalytic AI Solutions initiative will make the technology more accessible to SMEs, and support them in overcoming common barriers when adopting AI.
“We want AI to be accessible not just to large manufacturers, but also to our SMEs,” she said at the Industrial Transformation Asia-Pacific (ITAP) event at the Suntec Singapore Convention and Exhibition Centre.
“Through this initiative, manufacturers can access ready-to-deploy AI solutions to improve productivity, optimise efficiency and strengthen their competitiveness,” she added.
Under the initiative, Enterprise Singapore (EnterpriseSG) will work with trade associations and chambers and qualified vendors to offer a suite of solutions to SMEs, with some firms having already confirmed their interest.
The solutions will enable tasks such as the optimisation of product and component design, and the enhancement of production scheduling and predictive maintenance.
EnterpriseSG’s assistant managing director for manufacturing Wong Zeng Yi said: “AI is creating new possibilities for manufacturers to improve productivity, quality and responsiveness, while opening new revenue opportunities through faster innovation.
“We want to help more manufacturers embed AI into their core operations, so they can realise these gains at scale.”
Eligible SMEs will have their adoption of AI solutions co-funded by EnterpriseSG, which plans to extend the initiative to the logistics and wholesale trade sectors.
Another initiative announced at ITAP was a manufacturing jobs portal developed by the Singapore Manufacturing Federation.
Gan encouraged prospective employers and job seekers to sign up for the Manufacturing and Talent Connection Hub, which is expected to be operational later in 2026.
The manufacturing industry accounts for around 20% of Singapore’s gross domestic product, and employs about 12% of its workforce.
Industrial transformation has never been more important, Gan said, as manufacturers are operating in a more complex environment, with tight labour markets, intensifying competition for investments, and supply chains that are being reshaped by geopolitics.
Companies must also become more sustainable while remaining competitive, she added.
Gan said: “Advanced technologies such as robotics, digital twins and AI can help our manufacturers raise productivity, strengthen competitiveness, and bring about skilled roles for our workforce.
“If we move decisively, Singapore can strengthen our position as a critical global node for advanced manufacturing, where companies develop new technologies and engineering capabilities, deploy them at scale, and contribute to global manufacturing.”
A set of national AI missions, namely in advanced manufacturing, connectivity, finance and healthcare, was announced by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong earlier at Budget 2026.
This came alongside the creation of a National AI Council, chaired by PM Wong, to help Singapore harness AI as a strategic advantage.
The advanced manufacturing mission aims to reimagine the industry to grow its output and productivity.
This involves advancing product and process innovation, anchoring best-in-class factories in Singapore, and building a base of industrial AI companies that develop AI solutions locally and export them to the rest of the world.
Gan said the AI Centre of Excellence for Manufacturing, jointly established by A*STAR and the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry in September 2024, has been an important enabler of this mission.
Companies including drinks producer Coca-Cola and tech manufacturer Philips had signed on to collaborate with the centre at its launch.
In all, Gan said the centre has collaborated with 30 manufacturers in sectors including aerospace, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals and energy, ranging from local firm Sunningdale Tech to the multinational Rockwell Automation.
It has also completed 23 projects that deployed AI solutions to companies.
Gan said the centre will now enter its next phase and “deepen its capabilities to tackle more complex and mission-critical manufacturing problems, supporting end-to-end AI-enabled transformation and scaling AI adoption to the broader base of manufacturers”.
She added: “It will also draw more extensively on the strengths of our research and innovation ecosystem, working with our institutes of higher learning, frontier AI start-ups and technology providers to develop relevant, industry-ready AI solutions.”

articles.title: Indonesia haze threatens tiny bugs that power palm oil output - The Straits Times
articles.summary: Indonesia haze threatens tiny bugs that power palm oil output  The Straits Times
articles.full_text:
KUALA LUMPUR – The smog blanketing parts of South-east Asia is threatening an army of tiny-but-crucial workers in the region’s palm industry – beetles that pollinate the trees and help keep the world supplied with the most-consumed vegetable oil.
Dense smoke and reduced sunlight due to Indonesia’s forest fires can disrupt the activity of weevils carrying pollen from male to female flowers of oil palms, according to the Indonesian Oil Palm Research Institute. Such disturbances have previously been linked to a decline of as much as 20% in the share of flowers that grow into palm fruit, it said, and could once again shrink oil supplies.
Indonesia is suffering its worst fire season in over a decade. The resulting haze has disrupted everyday life, agricultural activity and transport in the country. The crisis has been exacerbated by a powerful El Nino weather pattern that has prolonged drought conditions and raised concerns that adverse impacts on palm yields will start emerging in 2027.
The threat of reduced pollination adds a layer of risk to an already grim supply outlook for the global palm market.
On top of the El Nino impact, the world’s top grower Indonesia is channelling more vegetable oil into biofuels, tightening supplies available for food and other uses and potentially raising costs for consumers. The US Department of Agriculture has forecast palm oil stockpiles to fall to a nine-year low in the 2026-27 season.
The ongoing haze may reduce the weevils’ ability to pollinate effectively, said Agus Eko Prasetyo, a crop-protection researcher at IOPRI, who also studied the insects during Indonesia’s devastating fires and haze in 2015. At the time, visits by weevils to female flowers plunged, possibly because of dimmed sunlight and other environmental changes, he said.
“A plantation may still have an adequate population of pollinating weevils, but pollination efficiency can decline if the insects become less active in moving between flowers,” Prasetyo said, adding it was too soon to measure the impact of the 2026 smog.
During the regional haze crisis of 2015, IOPRI observed a 5%-20% reduction in the proportion of fruits that developed from flowers. Poorer so-called “fruit set” can mean less oil-bearing growth. And because bunches take five to six months to mature after pollination, any impact would only show up in harvests around March or April, Prasetyo said.
Impaired pollination can also leave fruit underdeveloped and seedless, resulting in lighter bunches, or in severe cases, causing entire bunches to fail, according to researchers at the Malaysian Palm Oil Board. That could mean less oil extracted and potentially millions in lost revenue, they said, underscoring the critical role that the weevils play in boosting yields and productivity.
The insects were brought from Cameroon to Malaysia in the early 1980s, replacing the expensive and labour-intensive practice of pollinating palms by hand. They were introduced to neighbouring Indonesia soon after and have since become the most important insect pollinator of oil palms in the world’s two biggest growers.
On Indonesia and Malaysia’s vast plantations, where ageing trees and stagnant yields are already a cause for concern, the combination of haze-impaired weevils and El Nino-induced water stress may extend the impact on productivity long after the skies clear, scientists at IOPRI said.
“El Nino and haze can create a double impact on oil palm productivity,” Prasetyo said. “The combined effects of drought and haze could continue to influence palm oil production even after environmental conditions return to normal.” BLOOMBERG

articles.summary: Singaporeans Feeling the Pressure: Cost Concerns Rise as Household Optimism and Government Ratings Weaken - Blackbox Research Study  vietnamnews.vn
articles.full_text:
Blackbox’s latest SensingSG findings show affordability concerns rising amid global headwinds; workplace sentiment and the Good Governance Meter see notable falls.
Media OutReach Newswire – 22 October 2026 – Cost-of-living concerns have intensified and household optimism has weakened, reversing last quarter's improvement in economic sentiment, according to Blackbox Research's latest SensingSG national quarterly data. The Good Governance Meter, which aggregates public ratings of government performance across 26 community issues, fell four points to 69.
The survey of 1,533 Singapore citizens and permanent residents, conducted from 24–30 September, finds that half (50%) place cost of living among their two most important national and community issues, up from 41% in Q2. Confidence in Singapore's overall direction remains strong at 82%, although down from 87%.
Household Outlook Softens as Costs Bite
The financial outlook has weakened on several measures as questions of affordability once again rise to the surface:
- Family finances ahead: 51% expect to be better off in 12 months, down from 59% in Q2, while 21% expect to be worse off, up from 16%.
- Household progress: 46% feel financially better off than 12 months ago, down from 51% last quarter.
- National economic outlook: 30% expect conditions to worsen over the next 12 months, up from 23% in Q2.
Those aged 40–49 report particularly acute affordability pressure: 64% choose cost of living as a top-two issue, compared with 50% overall. Just 25% rate government performance on it good or excellent, against 42% overall.
The findings come amid higher household costs. August headline inflation was 2.3%, with electricity and gas prices 8.7% higher than a year earlier, reflecting the impact of elevated global energy prices.
"Recent global disruptions across key areas are starting to hit home hard," said David Black, Founder and CEO of Blackbox Research. "People experience the economy through their bills, their pay and their everyday spending. When everyday costs rise and the outlook at work feels less certain, positive national growth figures only offer so much reassurance."
Workplace Sentiment Weakens
Jobs and unemployment are a top-two concern for 21% of respondents, up from 18% in Q2.
Among employees, only 51% give a score of at least 8 out of 10 when asked whether they would recommend their organisation as a place to work, down 13 percentage points from 64% in Q2.
Official labour-market data released in September showed slower resident employment growth, rising retrenchments and fewer professional vacancies, while unemployment remained low. Concern about technological change was already evident in Q2, when 52% expressed concern about AI's impact on their career prospects.
Affordability and Fairness Weigh on Government Ratings
Government performance ratings declined across 20 of the 26 areas measured. Good or excellent ratings fell:
- Cost of living: from 51% to 42%.
- The gap between rich and poor: from 56% to 46%.
- Jobs and unemployment: from 62% to 56%.
Fieldwork followed the return of transboundary haze to Singapore, which was regarded as the biggest news story of the quarter among respondents (80% interest level), while the 8 September announcement on political salaries was the second biggest story (71% interest). Meanwhile, unpublished approval ratings tracked by Blackbox show that approval declined for 17 of the 19 political and institutional leaders tracked. Average approval across the group fell 2.9 percentage points, from 68.5% in Q2 to 65.6% in Q3.
"The Government faces a more demanding public mood," said Black. "Affordability pressures and uncertainty about future progress are resurfacing despite a solid macroeconomic backdrop. Confidence in Singapore's direction remains high. The balloon has not burst, but it has deflated."

articles.title: EV Manufacturing in Thailand: Who Builds What - Chiang Rai Times
articles.summary: EV Manufacturing in Thailand: Who Builds What  Chiang Rai Times
articles.full_text:
Thailand is shifting from a major vehicle assembly base toward electric vehicle production, with automakers opening factories, announcing investments, and weighing plans to build locally. But the evidence varies: a factory’s stated capacity, an approved investment, or a public plan doesn’t prove that a particular model is rolling off the line today.
As of October 2026, the picture includes Chinese EV makers with Thai production activity, Japanese automakers focused mainly on hybrids, and projects whose current status or model lineup remains unclear. Here’s what’s known about who builds what, and how to tell confirmed production from plans, capacity claims, and imports.
Key Takeaways
- Thailand’s EV plants are expanding, but announced capacity and approved investment don’t prove current production or output.
- BYD opened its Rayong plant in July 2024, with eventual capacity of 150,000 vehicles annually, according to the Thailand Board of Investment.
- Thailand’s BOI confirms Neta V production; Changan began production in 2025, though current model lists remain unclear.
- Hybrid and gas-powered vehicle assembly shouldn’t be mistaken for confirmed BEV production by GWM, MG, Toyota, Honda, or Isuzu.
- EV3 and EV3.5 incentives require domestic production to offset imports, and 2026 rule changes adjusted deadlines and production credits.
EV Manufacturing in Thailand: Who Builds What
Thailand’s EV story includes operating assembly lines, investment commitments, and vehicles that still arrive as imports. To compare automakers fairly, separate what a company has announced from what public evidence confirms it builds locally. This section reflects information available in October 2026, although some sources still don’t identify each model currently coming off the line.
What counts as an EV made in Thailand?
A vehicle is made in Thailand when the automaker manufactures or assembles it at a Thai facility. A finished vehicle shipped into the country is an import, even if the company has a local office, dealership network, or other vehicle production in Thailand.
The vehicle category matters, too. A battery electric vehicle (BEV) runs on electricity stored in a battery. A hybrid combines an electric motor with a combustion engine, while a conventional combustion vehicle relies on an engine. A company’s local hybrid or gas-powered assembly does not, by itself, prove that it builds BEVs in Thailand.
Factory announcements also need careful reading. A planned facility, investment approval, or stated annual capacity describes an intention or potential scale. None confirms that production has started, that a particular model is built there, or that the plant reaches its full capacity. Actual output requires separate evidence, such as a company or government statement confirming production.
The clearest production evidence, and the gaps
The strongest evidence names a Thai facility and confirms that production has begun. For example, Thailand’s Board of Investment identifies the Hozon factory as producing the Neta V in Thailand. BOI materials also report production activity by several other Chinese-backed automakers, including BYD, GAC Aion, Changan, Great Wall Motor, and SAIC MG. However, factory-level confirmation does not always establish which models are currently assembled.
That distinction matters for Japanese automakers as well. Toyota and Honda have substantial vehicle assembly in Thailand, but their hybrid production should not be counted as confirmed BEV manufacturing. Isuzu’s D-Max BEV has been associated with a Thai production plan; a plan alone does not verify that production began or continued.
For this article, confirmed production means a credible public source links a named vehicle to manufacturing or assembly in Thailand. When a source confirms a factory or production start but omits its model lineup, the brand’s activity can be noted without guessing which EVs it builds. Likewise, announced plans, capacity figures, and imported models remain separate categories.
Public sources available for this October 2026 overview don’t provide a complete, current Thai-built model list for every brand. The evidence is therefore strongest where a source names both a model and production, and more limited where it refers only to a factory, a company, or a future commitment.
Chinese EV makers are turning Thailand into a production base
Chinese automakers are building a larger manufacturing presence in Thailand, but factory announcements don’t always reveal which models currently roll off local lines. The distinction matters: reported capacity describes a plant’s potential scale, not its actual output or a confirmed model lineup.
BYD and GAC Aion have set up in Rayong
The Thailand Board of Investment identifies BYD’s Rayong factory as opening in 2024, with reported capacity of 150,000 vehicles a year. That figure is a plant capacity claim, not evidence that BYD currently produces that many vehicles. The BOI material available also doesn’t reliably identify which BYD models are assembled there, so a Thai-built model list can’t be confirmed from that source.
GAC Aion also has a factory in Rayong, with reported capacity of 50,000 vehicles annually. However, the available evidence doesn’t establish which models are currently assembled or confirm the factory’s full production status. In both cases, the location and stated capacity provide useful context, but they shouldn’t be treated as proof of current output. The BOI’s account of Thai EV manufacturing activity offers company-level information without a complete, up-to-date list of locally assembled models.
GWM and MG bring a wider mix of vehicles
Great Wall Motor’s Rayong plant has reported capacity of 80,000 vehicles a year. BOI material connects the plant with the Ora Good Cat, Haval, and Tank nameplates, but that doesn’t confirm that all three are currently made there. Nor should the entire lineup be described as BEVs: the names cover different vehicle types, including hybrids and other vehicles. The evidence supports a mixed-product factory, not a claim that every associated model is a battery electric vehicle assembled in Thailand.
SAIC MG also has local assembly activity, but the sources available don’t establish which MG BEV models are currently built in the country. MG’s Thai vehicle production should therefore be kept separate from confirmed BEV production unless a source names a model and confirms its local assembly. Hybrid and combustion-engine vehicles made by the company don’t count as evidence of locally built BEVs.
Changan and Neta show different stages of localization
BOI sources place Changan’s production activity in Thailand in 2025. They confirm the company has moved into local production, but don’t identify models verified as assembled at its Thai facility. As a result, Changan belongs in the group of manufacturers with reported production activity, while its locally built model lineup remains unconfirmed.
Neta has a more specific model reference. The BOI identifies Neta V production at Hozon’s Thai factory, providing evidence that links a named EV to local manufacturing. Its announcement on Hozon’s Thai production supports that model reference, but it doesn’t establish the factory’s current output. Capacity estimates for Neta differ across sources, so they shouldn’t be presented as settled figures. The confirmed Neta V reference is more useful than an uncertain capacity claim, though it still doesn’t prove how many vehicles the plant currently produces.
Japanese automakers are moving at a different pace
Japanese automakers have a long history of vehicle production in Thailand, but that does not make every local factory an EV plant. As of October 2026, the evidence points to Toyota and Honda prioritizing hybrids while evaluating EV production, while Isuzu has confirmed production of an electric pickup. The distinction is whether a source confirms a working BEV line or only describes a broader investment or future plan.
Toyota and Honda focus on hybrids while weighing BEVs
Thailand’s Board of Investment describes Toyota and Honda as focused on hybrid activity in the country, with EV production under consideration. That reflects a different pace from manufacturers whose Thai BEV production is already confirmed. The BOI’s account of Japanese automakers’ plans supports the distinction between current hybrid activity and possible EV production.
For Toyota, the available evidence does not identify a BEV model currently assembled in Thailand. For Honda, BOI materials discuss investment to adapt production lines for hybrid, mild-hybrid, and EV platforms, but do not confirm a locally built Honda BEV by model. That language signals preparation or consideration, not proof that a specific electric vehicle is rolling off a Thai line.
Factory upgrades and platform investments can support several types of vehicles. They do not establish that a particular BEV is in production. Toyota and Honda should therefore be counted for their confirmed hybrid activity, not described as Thai BEV manufacturers without model-level evidence. The available public information does not confirm a working BEV line for either company as of October 2026.
Isuzu’s D-Max BEV has moved beyond an announced plan
Isuzu’s case has stronger production evidence. The company unveiled the D-Max BEV in 2024 and announced plans to build it in Thailand for export to some European markets. At the time, the start date was a plan, not proof that production had begun.
That status changed in 2025. In an official production update, Isuzu said production of the left-hand-drive D-Max BEV for Europe had commenced. The company also said shipments to major European markets were scheduled for the third quarter of 2025. This confirms that production started, rather than leaving the vehicle at the announcement stage.

| Construction of a social housing project in Hà Tĩnh Province. Property prices have been falling recently on high interest rates and weak buyer absorption. — VNA/VNS Photo Hữu Quyết | 
HÀ NỘI — The real estate market needs greater transparency, tighter controls on speculation and a shift towards affordable housing to restore buyer confidence after years of rapid price increases, experts have said.
Although supply has improved, transactions have weakened as housing prices remain beyond the reach of a majority of homebuyers, highlighting a growing mismatch between available properties and actual demand.
The Ministry of Construction also reported that more than 59,000 commercial housing units were eligible for sale in the third quarter, along with more than 216,000 social housing units. Total property transactions exceeded 92,000, down year-on-year and about 8 per cent lower than the previous quarter.
While more properties are entering the market, supply remains concentrated in mid-range and high-end segments.
Other figures of the Vietnam Real Estate Association showed that the market had recorded about 98,000 property units launched for sale in the first half of 2026, up 50 per cent from a year earlier.
However, the primary market recorded only about 48,000 transactions during the same period. The absorption rate fell to 49 per cent from 62 per cent a year earlier.
The association’s vice president Nguyễn Văn Đính said high land-use costs, rising construction expenses and financing pressures made it difficult for developers to reduce prices. Lengthy project approval procedures also added to borrowing costs, which were reflected in selling prices.
Speculative buying had further distorted the market, with some investors using borrowed money to acquire properties in anticipation of short-term gains rather than to meet housing needs, he said.
Trần Quang Trung, business development director at OneHousing, said the market had experienced rapid price increases in 2024-25 amid limited supply, relatively affordable borrowing costs and the return of speculative capital.
Rising prices at newly launched projects also established higher benchmarks for the secondary market, where short-term investors buying and reselling properties within three to six months contributed to further increases, he said.
However, property prices have fallen by around 15-20 per cent since the beginning of 2026, Trung said, adding that price movements varied by location, property segment and sellers’ financial positions.
A recent report by Đất Xanh Services' Institute of Economics, Finance and Real Estate Research showed that primary housing prices in fell by 5-20 per cent in the third quarter from the previous quarter across most regions and property segments, as high interest rates and weak buyer absorption weighed on the market.
Economist Ngô Trí Long said higher interest rates could further weaken purchasing power and market liquidity, putting particular pressure on developers and investors heavily reliant on borrowing.
Transparency, affordability key to recovery
| Apartments buildings along Sài Gòn River in HCM City. — VNA/VNS Photo Hồng Đạt | 
Hoàng Thu Hằng, deputy director of the Ministry of Construction’s Department of Housing and Real Estate Market Management, said high property prices reflected a combination of land costs, compensation and site clearance, construction, infrastructure investment, marketing and financing expenses as well as speculation.
Hằng said the ministry was working with local authorities and businesses to improve the national housing and real estate market information system with better access to reliable data to allow buyers to check project legal status and assess supply and demand in individual areas before making purchasing decisions.
A more transparent database would also help developers identify actual demand and enable regulators to monitor market developments, detect unusual price movements and respond to potential distortions, she said.
Authorities are working to resolve obstacles affecting more than 5,000 property projects, with more than 3,500, or about 71 per cent already addressed.
The government has set a target of completing 97,271 social housing units in 2026 as part of a goal of nearly 900,000 units for 2026-30.
Expanding social housing, affordable commercial housing and rental accommodation is expected to help address the gap between available products and household purchasing power, Hằng said.
Hằng also urged developers to shift their focus from maximising profits on individual properties to improving cash flow and accelerating sales.
For homeseekers, Hằng advised assessing a property's value, location and suitability against their financial capacity rather than waiting indefinitely for the market to reach its lowest points while investors without immediate housing needs should remain cautious.
According to Đính, it is necessary to restructuring supply towards more affordable homes, shortening administrative procedures and improving access to reasonably priced credit for homeseekers with real demand.
He also called for stronger legal measures to prevent price manipulation and specualtion. — VNS

TEMPO.CO, Jakarta - The Chair of the Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (Kadin), Anindya Bakrie, encourages business actors to increase exports and strengthen company fundamentals amid ongoing global economic uncertainty.
According to him, the business sector must not only survive but also sharpen its competitive edge to contend with rival nations.
"The business sector must refocus on economic fundamentals. Because we not only need to survive but also succeed in improving competitiveness," Anindya said during a press conference ahead of Kadin’s National Leadership Meeting in Jakarta on Thursday, October 22, 2026.
He assesses that Indonesia's economic fundamentals remain relatively robust. Over the past 30 years, Indonesia's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth has averaged roughly five percent. Although it experienced sharp contractions in 1998 and 2001–2002, he noted that the domestic economy is currently growing at 5.6 percent.
"The government and business sector hope this growth can increase to 6 percent," he said.
However, Anindya warns that Indonesia's competitiveness needs continuous strengthening as it still trails several neighboring peers. Alongside internal corporate improvements, he hopes the government will broaden the distribution of state spending, particularly to the regions, and enact policies that stimulate domestic consumption.
He stated that domestic consumption plays a crucial role in anchoring trade activities. Consequently, the economic pressures currently confronting the middle class also warrant serious government attention.
"Especially, we must focus on the middle class that is under pressure," he remarked.
In navigating present economic conditions, Anindya mentioned that Kadin is concentrating on two priorities: boosting exports and strengthening economic fundamentals to attract higher investment flows. This investment strategy includes both the capital market and foreign direct investment (FDI).
Anindya expressed optimism that domestic investment realization will continue its upward trend. He estimates its total value to reach around Rp2,000 trillion this year and potentially rise to Rp2,500 trillion next year. "This is very likely to happen," he stated.
Anindya also urges business owners to stay calm when confronting global headwinds. He encourages companies to scale up exports, particularly those that have already established an international footprint, while carefully managing cash flow to maintain operational resilience and enhance market competitiveness.

| According to EBC Financial Group, the surge in goods imports reflects Vietnam's growing investment cycle. | 
 Imports are being transformed into production capacity.
 In its newly released report on Vietnam's import situation, EBC Financial Group (EBC) suggests that the strong increase in imports reflects a notable aspect of the economy : the expansion of investment and the enhancement of production capacity.
 In the first nine months of 2026, Vietnam's exports reached US$434.3 billion, a 24.5% increase compared to the same period last year; imports reached US$452.72 billion, a 36.7% increase. The difference between exports and imports resulted in a trade deficit of US$19.42 billion.
 Notably, production materials accounted for 94.1% of total import value during the period. During the same period, industrial production in the third quarter increased by 14.8%, asset accumulation increased by 21.39%, and the manufacturing sector production index increased by 12.9%.
 Foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows also reinforced the trend of expanding production. FDI disbursed in the first nine months reached US$21.07 billion, with 82.6% concentrated in the processing and manufacturing sector.
 The data reveals an increasingly clear link between imports, investment, and production: imported machinery, equipment, and raw materials support investment activities; investment helps expand production capacity; and this new capacity is gradually reflected in industrial output.
 However, the report also emphasizes that increased imports of production materials do not necessarily mean that every dollar imported generates a corresponding economic benefit. The ultimate effectiveness depends on the ability to utilize production capacity, labor productivity, the proportion of value added created domestically, and the ability to consume the products in the global market.
 The current import structure shows a trend towards expanding investment and production. However, the effectiveness of this cycle will only be truly confirmed when new capacity helps to improve productivity, increase domestic value, and generate additional export revenue.
 How much did Vietnam gain from the investment cycle?
 In the next phase, the economic efficiency generated by investment capital will become a more important factor, rather than just looking at the scale of capital invested or the amount of machinery and raw materials imported, EBC predicts.
 One notable difference is the trade performance between the domestic economic sector and the foreign-invested sector. According to the EBC report, in the first nine months of 2026, the domestic economic sector had a trade deficit of US$34.28 billion, while the FDI sector had a trade surplus of US$14.86 billion.
 EBC Financial Group argues that this disparity poses a long-term problem for the economy.
 Production capacity can increase rapidly, but the extent to which domestic businesses benefit depends on their ability to participate more deeply in the supply chain, access technology, develop services, and expand operations into higher value-added stages.
 Therefore, a sustainable investment cycle needs to be accompanied by higher productivity, greater export capacity, and an improved rate of domestic value added.
 "The assessment of the next phase of the investment cycle in Vietnam needs to focus on actual output, value created domestically, and foreign exchange earnings from imported machinery, equipment, and production materials," the report states.
 If export volumes gradually catch up with import growth as new capacity comes online, the current trade deficit will have a different meaning compared to a deficit primarily driven by consumer demand. Conversely, if the conversion of investment into export capacity is slow, pressure on capital and the balance of payments may increase.
 Sana Ur Rehman, Senior Market Analyst at EBC Financial Group, commented: “The Q3 GDP figures show that Vietnam’s investment cycle is generating real output. However, September manufacturing data suggests that to maintain this pace, businesses may have to operate in a more challenging cost environment. Therefore, the quality and efficiency of growth are becoming increasingly important.”
 Although the Q3/2026 data further reinforces evidence that the import cycle is directly supporting investment and industrial activity in Vietnam, Q4 will show how sustainable this trend is.
 “The third-quarter figures show more clearly that the import cycle is supporting investment and industrial activity. The question in the final quarter is whether export demand, productivity and domestic value added can keep pace given that input costs and capital costs remain high,” Rehman added.
 For the remainder of 2026, EBC suggests there are five key indicators to watch.

articles.title: Turning Payment Data Into Trade Finance for SMEs - Fintech Singapore
articles.summary: Turning Payment Data Into Trade Finance for SMEs  Fintech Singapore
articles.full_text:
Linking payment systems with digital identity systems among other services and facilities can help Asian economies expand digital trade and narrow the trade finance gap facing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), according to a new paper by the Asian Development Bank Institute (ADBI).
In particular, pairing payment data with commercial, logistics, customs, and financial records, can not only allow SMEs to get paid more efficiently but also allow them to obtain the funding they need to produce, ship, and sell goods internationally.
SMEs bear disproportionate frictions in cross-border trade because many costs associated with payments, compliance, documentation, and credit assessment are fixed at the transaction or customer level. Verifying a new customer, screening a payment, examining trade documents, and conducting due diligence require substantial resources regardless of the size of the transaction, weighing heaviest on smaller firms.
In addition, SMEs often struggle to obtain trade finance as they often lack collateral, have short credit histories, incomplete financial statements, and less established relationships with financial institutions. Consequently, banks often find it difficult to assess their creditworthiness or verify underlying transactions, particularly when parties operate across different legal and regulatory systems.
At the same time, cross-border trade remains heavily fragmented and inefficient. A single transaction generates orders, contracts, invoices, transport documents, insurance records, customs declarations, delivery confirmations, payment instructions, and settlement records, often maintained separately by firms, banks, logistics providers, insurers, and authorities. This fragmentation forces repeated data entry, verification, and reconciliation.
Connecting digital payments to trade finance, verified invoices, digital identity, and logistics data may ease these issues, the report says. In particular, greater interoperability could allow verified commercial activity to generate a more usable digital transaction record. With appropriate authorization, a lender might confirm that an order was placed, goods were shipped, customs procedures were completed, and previous payments were made as agreed. Such information could complement conventional financial statements and collateral when assessing credit risk.
Programmable payments could further strengthen this connection by allowing payment to be released when specified conditions are satisfied, for example, when an authorized electronic document is presented or when trusted data confirms that goods have reached an agreed stage of the transaction.
Recommendations
The ADBI report outlines a framework for capturing these opportunities. First, it recommends that cross-border payment reform start with solid domestic groundwork instead of relying on a specific technology. Key priorities include dependable domestic payment systems, shared data and identity standards, legal acceptance of electronic trade documents, balanced compliance, clear payment and foreign exchange costs, and wide access for regulated financial institutions and payment providers.
The next step involves expanding proven cross-border arrangements where there is clear economic demand. QR merchant payments, fast payment system linkages, account-to-account transfers, improvements to correspondent banking, and local currency transaction arrangements can be developed progressively along important trade, tourism, and remittance corridors. Regional cooperation should support interoperability without requiring every economy to adopt a single payment model.
Payment connectivity should then be linked with electronic invoices and trade documents, customs and logistics data, foreign exchange services, and working capital and trade finance facilities. Tokenized deposits and wholesale CBDC platforms should be pursued selectively where they provide a clear advantage over existing arrangements and where legal certainty, governance, liquidity, operational resilience, and interoperability can be established.
Finally, progress should be evaluated through outcomes for users rather than technical performance alone. Relevant indicators include total transaction costs, foreign exchange spreads, predictability and speed of access to funds, rejected or delayed payments, access to trade finance, and participation by SMEs and smaller financial institutions. The objective is not to replace existing systems with a single new infrastructure, but to create a more interoperable, resilient, and inclusive cross-border payment architecture, the report says.
Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in developing APAC contribute meaningfully to the region’s economy. According to the Asian Development Bank (ADB), these organizations represent an average of 99.8% of all enterprises, 67.6% of the workforce, and 38.7% of national economic output.
The ADB estimates that the global unmet demand for trade finance totaled approximately US$2.5 trillion in 2025, equivalent to about 10% of global trade.
Across APAC, governments, development banks, and trade organizations are working to reduce the trade finance gap through credit guarantees, subsidized export loans, and digitalization efforts.
ADB’s Trade and Supply Chain Finance Program (TSCFP) offers guarantees and loans to fill market gaps, support cross-border trade, and reinforce key supply chains. The program collaborates with commercial banks, corporations, industry groups, governments, and development institutions, backing more than 104,000 transactions worth US$74 billion since 2009.
In Singapore, the Enterprise Financing Scheme – Trade Loan (EFS-TL) assists local firms in obtaining short-term trade and working capital with government risk sharing. It covers 50% of eligible default risk for lenders, increasing to 70% for young firms or those in difficult markets.
Separately, Singapore’s Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) introduced TradeTrust in 2019, a framework that standardizes digital trade with improved security and legal certainty. It’s designed to cut inefficiencies and complexities in cross-border trade caused by traditional paper documents such as bills of lading.
